subject: Exec checkpoint: roadmap gaps + triage plan for QBR
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlashealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep — outstanding integration gaps and timeline

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for last week's demo. We're pulling together the QBR pack and I wanted to flag three outstanding areas the execs will ask about:

- Observability for per-request token costs across environments (hosted vs dedicated)
- Data residency SLA for EU PII workloads (audit evidence needed)
- Predictable throughput for our inference spikes (we saw throttling in the alpha test)

Can you share who on your side owns the remediation plans and whether there's a proposed timeline? We'd like to surface a concrete roll-forward in the QBR.

Attaching our QBR template for reference.

Elena
VP Product, Atlas Health

Attachment: atlas_qbr_template_v2.pptx (attachment)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlashealth.com>, Procurement <procure@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 18:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep — outstanding integration gaps and timeline

Team — forwarding Atlas's ask. Need concise owners, mitigations, and dates by EOD tomorrow so we can provide a roll-forward in the QBR. Quick plan below: 

1) Observability (cost breakdown): Marissa to propose a one-page telemetry deliverable and ETA.
2) Data residency / audit evidence: Lauren to confirm whether Private deployment artifacts + SOC-2 exports cover the ask; escalate to Security if not.
3) Throughput/throttling: Vivek to share short-term fences (burst configs, routing policy) and longer-term Dedicated capacity plan.

Please edit this doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/0B2QBR-gap-tracker (I'll drop the tracker there). I'm copying Elena so we can set expectations.

Karthik
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: QBR_gap_tracker.xlsx (placeholder)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep — outstanding integration gaps and timeline

Adding owners and provisional dates in the tracker. Short summary here: 

- Observability: Proposed deliverable: token-cost dashboard per route + example export (CSV). Owner: Marissa; ETA: 2027-05-18 (MVP), 2027-06-08 (polish). Rationale: Metrically answers exec ask.
- Data residency(Audit): Lauren to confirm artifacts; if gap, we'll produce an audit pack by 2027-05-21.
- Throughput: Vivek proposes burst policy + canary routing by 2027-05-11; Dedicated capacity recommendation by 2027-06-01.

Open question for execs: Do we commit to a specific Dedicated start date (customer wants a Q3 date). Recommend we present options + required contract/commit steps rather than a hard date.

Marissa
Director, Product Solutions

Quick update on audit artifacts:

- Private deployment artifacts: we have deployment manifests and KMS logs that cover EU residency for the workloads in scope.
- SOC-2 exports: available, but Atlas wants a simpler evidence packet. I've asked Security to prepare a 1-2 page summary + packaged logs for the specific systems.

If Security can confirm by 2027-05-10 we'll hit Marissa's 05-21 audit pack date. Security (cc) — can you confirm feasible delivery?

Lauren
VP, Security & Compliance

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep — outstanding integration gaps and timeline

Team — please see my plan below and what I'll deliver to the tracker by EOD: 

- Short term (stopgap): add routing policy that avoids small-instance throttling; set burst allowance to 2x for Atlas test accounts. ETA: 2027-05-11.
- Canary: run a single-region canary with KV-cache warmup and TLS connection reuse enabled; ETA: 2027-05-18.
- Capacity rec: recommend Dedicated baseline with autoscale window; draft proposal for customer-facing commitment by 2027-05-25.

Notes for exec slide: we'll present two paths — "Mitigate quickly (config + routing)" vs "Guaranteed throughput (Dedicated commit)" with cost/lead time tradeoffs.

Vivek
Head of Serving Infrastructure
